title: Throughput tuning deep dive - continuous batching & scheduler knobs
summary: SE-led deep dive covering throughput tuning for BrightScale's inference workloads. Discussed continuous batching behavior, scheduler knobs (max_num_seqs, max_tokens, schedule windows), KV cache warmup and eviction patterns, quantization tradeoffs, and VPC/on-prem constraints. Agreed next steps: run a 24h benchmark with specified knobs, share suggested config, and schedule follow-up to review results.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-18
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Morris (Redwood SE), Liam Chen (BrightScale Infra Lead), Priya Rao (BrightScale ML Eng), Marta Silva (BrightScale SRE)

Summary (auto): SE walked through continuous batching and scheduler knobs, we looked at max_num_seqs and token limits, and discussed KV cache behavior and quantization tradeoffs. Action items captured.

[00:00] Sofia Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Ethan is going to lead the deep dive today, just to set expectations we'll go 45-ish minutes and leave time for Q&A.
[00:12] Ethan Morris: Thanks Sofia. Hi all, quick intro, I'm Ethan, runtime perf at Redwood. Liam, Priya, Marta, thanks for sharing your workload notes ahead of time - that helped.
[00:25] Liam Chen: Yeah no problem, we put together request distribution and token histograms.
[00:32] Priya Rao: Sorry, one thing, we're running mixed short-chat and long-completion workloads, 60% sub-64 tokens, 30% 64-256, 10% longer tails.
[00:44] Ethan Morris: Perfect, that distribution tells me continuous batching will help a lot for the short-chat while not tanking latency for the long ones if we tune max_num_seqs and token caps.
[00:58] Marta Silva: Quick question - we're in a VPC with private deploy, some constraints on outbound to metrics collection, does that change the advice?
[01:07] Ethan Morris: It affects telemetry but not core scheduler knobs. We'll share a config that works for private deploy. Just ensure the agent can access the shared s3 bucket or internal metrics sink.

[03:15] Ethan Morris: Ok let's go into continuous batching basics — Redwood's scheduler accumulates requests into an in-memory batch window and has a couple of levers: max_num_seqs (how many concurrent sequences per GPU batch), batch_window_ms (how long to wait to fill a batch), and max_tokens_per_batch. Common pattern: for chat-heavy workloads set max_num_seqs 6-12, batch_window 6-12ms to trade a few ms of latency for 2-4x throughput.
[03:48] Priya Rao: Is there a rule-of-thumb for picking max_num_seqs vs batch_window?
[03:54] Ethan Morris: Yes — if p50 latency target is tight (<60ms) keep batch_window small (3-6ms) and lower max_num_seqs; if you can tolerate slightly higher p50 for much better throughput, increase max_num_seqs. Also watch p95, because tails can explode when long requests block KV cache or fill GPU memory.

[06:10] Liam Chen: We saw a weird pattern where p95 spikes every few minutes. Any ideas?
[06:16] Ethan Morris: Two likely causes: KV cache warmup/eviction and straggler long sequences that block scheduling. If your model uses large KV state and not enough eviction, you'll hit memory pressure which serializes some requests. We can look at per-device kv_cache_hit metrics.
[06:34] Marta Silva: Our infra shows periodic GC-like memory reclaim; might be cache churn.
[06:40] Ethan Morris: Right, tuning kv_cache size and TTL is important. For mixed workloads, enabling prefix KV caching on frequently repeated prompts gives a big perf win. But be careful with TTL if you have strong data residency requirements in VPC.

[09:05] Ethan Morris: On quantization — 4-bit quant works great for throughput but watch for regression on certain instruction-heavy models. We recommend running eval prompts when enabling 4-bit or q4_0 forms; if quality drops, try mixed precision (8-bit packed) or per-layer selective quant.
[09:28] Priya Rao: We've tried q4 and saw minor hallucination uptick on our safety prompts. Should we avoid quant for the safety-critical route?
[09:36] Ethan Morris: For safety-critical routes, prefer higher precision or conservative quantization profiles. Redwood supports per-route quant settings so you can have high-precision model for the safety path and quantized variant for bulk benches.

[12:00] Ethan Morris: Let's talk concrete knob values. Given your token distribution (Priya's histogram), for the 60% short chat I'd start with: max_num_seqs=8, batch_window_ms=8, max_tokens_per_batch=2048, token_limit_per_request=512. This should push throughput while keeping p50 in the low 70s ms.
[12:25] Liam Chen: If we raise max_num_seqs from 8 to 12, what happens to p95?
[12:30] Ethan Morris: Expect p95 to rise — maybe double — because more sequences in batch increase tail risk especially when long sequences arrive. To mitigate, set token_limit_per_request to cap long tails and enable preemptive scheduling for sequences > token_threshold (e.g., route >512 tokens to a separate queue/pool).

[14:50] Priya Rao: You mentioned scheduler preemption — how do we route long requests to a different pool?
[14:55] Ethan Morris: You can configure routing rules in Redwood: policy checks request.size_tokens and route to 'long' pool with lower concurrency but dedicated GPUs. That keeps short-p99 tight. It's a common pattern for mixed workloads.

[18:10] Ethan Morris: Important: for on-prem/VPC set the system-level ulimits and cgroup memory to avoid OOM kills when scheduling max_num_seqs high. We saw a customer bump max_num_seqs to 16 and hit OOM on smaller instance types.
[18:34] Marta Silva: We're on A30-type nodes with 48GB RAM — is 16 safe?
[18:40] Ethan Morris: For 48GB it's borderline depending on model size and KV usage. Better to test with incremental increases and monitor GPU memory free and kv_cache_bytes.

[22:00] Ethan Morris: Now about KV cache behavior — observed patterns: cold-starts incur higher latency until hot entries accumulate; eviction due to client-side TTL or memory pressure will cause periodic latency spikes. For your workload, set kv_cache_ttl to 10-15 minutes for chat sessions, and enable periodic pre-warm for top 100 prompt prefixes during business hours.
[22:33] Priya Rao: Prewarm — can we seed cache from prior logs?
[22:38] Ethan Morris: Yes, Redwood supports a seeding API to inject common prefixes into cache at boot. We can share a script.

[25:12] Liam Chen: Any gotchas for VPC / on-prem metric collection? We restrict outbound, and sometimes agent can't reach the telemetry endpoint.
[25:21] Sofia Patel: We usually provide an offline collector and a metrics-forwarder that can drop logs to your internal bucket or syslog. We'll include that in the private deployment checklist.

[28:20] Ethan Morris: Bench design proposal — run a 24-hour steady-state run with your mix, two conditions: baseline (current defaults) and tuned (max_num_seqs=8, batch_window=8ms, token_cap=512, kv_cache_ttl=12m, quantization=8bit). Capture p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, GPU util, kv_cache_hitrate, memory headroom. Also run an extreme tail test where 2% of requests are 2000+ tokens to see preemption behavior.
[29:05] Priya Rao: That sounds good. For the quantization test, we'll also include q4 on a separate branch to compare quality regressions.

[33:12] Ethan Morris: A few quick commands for the benchmark (demo): 
- ./run_bench --profile mixed --duration 24h --max_num_seqs 8 --batch_window_ms 8 --token_limit 512 --out logs/tuned
- collect: prom_pull redwood_gpu_metrics, kv_cache_metrics, and request_traces at 1s resolution.

[36:00] Marta Silva: On rollout strategy, we should canary tuned settings on 10% traffic for 6 hours then ramp. Any automation?
[36:08] Ethan Morris: Redwood Console supports traffic-weighted rollouts; we can add automated rollback if p95 > baseline * 1.5. We'll send a sample policy.

[39:45] Liam Chen: About security/compliance, might need to ensure KV cache TTL aligns with data-retention policy and KMS keys live in our HSM. Can Redwood work with customer-managed KMS in VPC?
[39:56] Sofia Patel: Yes, private deployments support customer-managed KMS/HSM and we can restrict metadata leakage. We'll send the integration docs.

[43:00] Ethan Morris: Quick note on observability — instrument request-level metadata with route, model_variant, batch_id, seq_count, and kv_cache_hit so you can slice the p95 by batch size and route. That makes tuning much easier.

[46:20] Priya Rao: Any tuning heuristics for token_limit_per_request?
[46:25] Ethan Morris: Set token_limit to cap requests that would blow up batch memory; typical values 512-1024 depending on model. For Llama- or Mistral-like models, conservative 512 is fine. Increase if your long-tail use-cases require it and route those to separate pool.

[49:10] Sofia Patel: Ok, recap and next steps. Ethan will share the reference config and bench script by tomorrow. Liam will run the 24h benchmark and upload logs; we'll meet to review on 2026-06-24. I'll send the private deploy/KMS docs and the canary rollback policy.
[49:34] Liam Chen: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[49:40] Marta Silva: Thanks, helpful.
[49:45] Priya Rao: Thanks, talk soon.
[50:00] Ethan Morris: Thanks, bye.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings ("kv cash" sometimes), filler words, and timestamps approximate.
